structured_output.summary: Phase 8 (Qualification and delivery) is in strong shape for the reviewed source cf44fb56. docs/checks/phase-08.json records exactly the 77 commands that tools/check_phase.py:175-204 defines for phase 8, every one with exit_code 0 and timeout false, bound to the reviewed fingerprint with source_unchanged true. The contract suite is complete and verifiable: 448/448 frozen operations implemented, offline-contract-verified and option-complete, 3,820 export capabilities closed, and all 448 recorded Rust namespaces are now crate-rooted (the prior namespace-rooting finding is genuinely fixed). Package qualification extracts the real .crate, enforces the include policy, compares packaged LICENSE/NOTICE bytes, runs minimal/all-feature unit tests, examples and doctests from the extracted archive, and executes the standalone 3,820-probe consumer on both 1.89.0 and 1.99.0. The dependency gate fetches RustSec HEAD fresh (999ec89d), audits 206 packages with warnings denied, and its policy checker is protected by regressions that reject graph exclusions, advisory ignores, license exceptions and non-crates.io sources. Adversarial/parser evidence is concrete: ADVERSARIAL.md's claims match the nine tests actually present in parser_qualification.rs. Platform labels are honest - musl native, a retained GNU 1.89.0 all-feature matrix receipt, and explicitly compile-only ARM64/Apple/Windows with transport exclusions asserted. Live evidence is candidly bounded (17 verified, 3 permission_prerequisite, 2 service_contract_rejection, 426 unverified, each with an explicit reason) and nothing is promoted from offline parity. The change under review (splitting native jobs into a workflow_dispatch-only file, bounded redacted dependency diagnostics, no-run doctest and GNU wording precision) has retained before/after logs showing the new guards failing first and passing after. Remaining gaps: the delivery milestone itself (push of the reviewed source, terminal successful remote run, exact v0.1.0 tag) is still pending by construction, live mutation/cleanup chains have no successful service evidence, and the newly added dependency diagnostics have a few real but low-severity defects. No blocker or high findings.

findings.description: Phase 8's acceptance evidence includes "push reviewed commits to origin", and docs/PHASES.md:18 makes a successful delivery part of the phase. The reviewed source cf44fb56 is uncommitted (origin/main is at 8034e36), the only --require-clean archive proofs bind releaseCommit 8034e36 (docs/checks/release-source-8034e36/*), run 12 at 8034e36 passed all 47 required jobs and all 77 commands but never reached terminal success because three optional native jobs stayed pending (docs/checks/phase-08-ci-run-12/run-status.json:10-31), and release_tag v0.1.0 remains local only. This is recorded honestly and is structurally post-review, but phase 8 cannot be marked complete on this review alone.
findings.required_fix: After accepting this review, commit and push the reviewed source, run both --require-clean package proofs on 1.89.0 and 1.99.0 against the new commit, retain a terminal-successful source-bound Forgejo run for the dispatch-split workflow, push the v0.1.0 tag at the exact published source and verify its remote peeled commit, then refresh the private-material scan and set the phase-8 milestones from the actual artifacts.

findings.description: Milestone 8's "controlled live workflows and cleanup" is only partly satisfied. 426 of 448 operations were never attempted live, and both mutation entry points (iam.scopes.create, gateway.workspaces.provision) were rejected with 400, so the entire downstream chain - scope read/update/delete, absence verification, workspace archival and owned-binding cleanup - is unexercised and live_evidence reports cleanupState "not_needed" only because nothing was created (docs/checks/phase-08.json:1446). The cause of the two 400s is unestablished and an SDK request-shape defect is explicitly not excluded (tools/qualification.py:27). This is labelled accurately everywhere I checked and nothing is promoted on offline parity, so it is a scope limitation rather than a misstatement.
findings.required_fix: Keep both operations and every dependent mutation/cleanup path explicitly live-unqualified. Before any stable promotion, obtain private diagnostics for the two 400 responses, reconcile the traffic-derived IAM and Gateway provisioning request contracts against a vendor specification, and record a new source-bound receipt that actually exercises create/read/update/delete plus confirmed cleanup.

findings.description: The new partial-failure receipt is not universal. main() catches only ValueError, OSError and subprocess.SubprocessError, and the __main__ handler at line 231 catches only ValueError, OSError and TimeoutExpired. A KeyError from a malformed Cargo.lock package table (check_lock iterates lock['package'] and indexes package['name'] at lines 30-31), an AttributeError, or an exception raised while exec'ing scripts/check-native-exports.py at lines 104-106 therefore produces a traceback with no partial report and no bounded child tails. docs/CI.md:126-129 and docs/phase-status.json:1084 describe the guarantee without that qualification.
findings.required_fix: Broaden the handler in main() to BaseException-excluding KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit (or at minimum add KeyError, TypeError, AttributeError, StopIteration and json.JSONDecodeError), keep writing the partial receipt and bounded diagnostics on every path, and add a regression that injects a non-ValueError exception and asserts the failed report is still written.

findings.description: print_failure_diagnostics falls back to checks[-1:] when no recorded command has a nonzero exit code. Qualification can fail with every child succeeding - passed is also gated on unchanged (lockfile changed during the run) and zero (cargo-audit reported warnings) at lines 182-186 - and in that case the job log emits {"failed_command": <cargo-deny invocation>, "exit_code": 0}, naming a command that did not fail. That is actively misleading for the operator reading a failed CI job.
findings.required_fix: Only emit failed_command entries for records with a nonzero or null exit code; when the failure came from lockfileUnchanged or nonzero audit findings, print a distinct diagnostic that names the actual failing condition instead of relabelling the last successful command.

findings.description: The headline "no unexplained gaps" assurance is tautological. summary() counts rows whose liveReason is falsy, but project() assigns a non-empty reason on every branch (lines 120-134), so unexplainedGaps is structurally always 0 and the guard at line 172 can never fire. The real protection comes from the earlier raises at lines 112-130; the published metric adds no independent evidence while reading like a verified property in contracts/qualification.json and the phase records.
findings.required_fix: Either remove unexplainedGaps, or redefine it to something falsifiable - for example the count of rows whose liveAcceptance is not "verified" and whose reason is the generic "not executed by the controlled native probe set" default - and state that number explicitly in docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md.

findings.description: For the 1,086 schema capabilities the generated external consumer emits `{ let _ = scm_sdk::validation::parse("<Name>Schema", serde_json::Value::Null, Mode::Request); }` and discards the Result. An unregistered schema name would return Err and the probe would still exit 0, so the public-consumer evidence proves only that the entry point compiles and links, not that each named schema resolves. Enum and constant capabilities by contrast carry real assertions (for example line 2379). Schema registry coverage is independently established by tools/generate_models.py --verify-fixtures (1,086 public schemas, 27,216 typed cases) and tools/schema-oracle.mts, so this weakens one evidence source rather than leaving a gap.
findings.required_fix: Make the generated schema probes assert that the call fails for a schema-shape reason rather than an unknown-name reason (or expose a public is_known-style predicate and assert it), and regenerate contracts/native-probes/src/main.rs plus its recorded consumer hash.

findings.description: The GNU native execution claim cites the run-11 matrix receipt at source 72765d5, even though an equivalent 1.89.0 all-feature GNU receipt exists for the newer run 12 at 8034e36 (docs/checks/phase-08-ci-run-12/matrix-capture-receipt.json:8-23) and the reviewed source is cf44fb56. The document states the source commit explicitly so it is not misleading, but the delivery document points at the older of two retained receipts.
findings.required_fix: Point docs/PLATFORMS.md at the newest retained GNU matrix receipt, and after the reviewed source is pushed and re-run, update it to the receipt bound to the delivered commit.

findings.description: The gate recorded cargoTargetDir "/build/rust/target", an externally supplied CARGO_TARGET_DIR outside the repository. That is exactly the configuration that masked the run-10 nested-build-output defect, so the newly added default-target-directory behaviour in scripts/check-native-exports.py is exercised only by the separate proof (docs/checks/phase-08-default-cargo-proof.json) and the mocked subprocess test in tools/test_ci.py:124-156, not by the 77-command gate itself.
findings.required_fix: Have the phase gate record whether CARGO_TARGET_DIR was externally set, and run at least one gate execution (or a dedicated gate command) with it unset so the owned default path is covered by the source-bound report rather than only by a side receipt.
